newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom invests $63 million in cable.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom invests $63 million in cable.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG said Thursday it would invest about 100 million marks ($63 million) in a project to build the world's longest and largest-capacity submarine cable network.
Telekom said it was the largest investor with a 5 percent stake in the project. The network will be built by 90 telecommunications companies from four continents at a cost of $1.3 billion.

The fiber-optic submarine cable is being built to meet burgeoning communications traffic in the fast-growing region and stretch from the South Pacific to the North Atlantic across Asia and the Middle East.
The 23,600-mile network will be open to commercial traffic by the end of 1998.
The agreement to build the network was signed and announced on Wednesday in Singapore.
